informal_statement: For any element \( b \) in a finite set \( s \), if a property \( p(b) \) does not hold, then the corresponding function value \( g(b) \) is less than or equal to the supremum of a function defined over the set \( s \), which catters both the function \( f(b) \) when \( p(b) \) holds and the function \( g(b) \) when it does not.
informal_proof: Consider an arbitrary element \( b \) in the finite set \( s \). Given that \( b \) is an element of \( s \) and \( p(b) \) does not hold, we need to establish that \( g(b) \) is less than or equal to the supremum of a function over \( s \). Since \( p(b) \) is false, the function \( g(b) \) is utilized. The supremum of the function over \( s \) captures the least upper bound for all values of the function, encompassing both cases where \( p(b) \) holds and where it does not. Therefore, \( g(b) \), being one of these function values, must necessarily be less than or equal to the supremum. This holds for all elements \( b \) in \( s \) where \( p(b) \) does not hold, thereby establishing the desired inequality.
